deck_abundance.why: NOT APPLICABLE for this deck, and that is the finding. Fe's grid resolves ONE A(X) at fixed [Fe/H] (7.50 in the aux table, 7.46 as the departures were actually computed), so a single scalar is the whole story. Al's resolves THIRTY-ONE (4.43-7.43 at the solar node, 454,466 aux rows against Fe's 15,229), and the departures genuinely DIFFER between them — interpolating at A = 6.20 / 6.43 / 6.70 returns three different departure blocks (sha256 d54fb26c / 58e03eb4 / ef995777), where the same test on Fe returns one. So Al interpolates at the abundance being synthesised; there is no single deck abundance to record. See `gerber_nlte.abundance_axis`.
